Let  
\[
\mathbf d=\mathbf c-\mathbf a.
\]
Then \(\mathbf c=\mathbf a+\mathbf d\), so
\[
\mathbf c\times \mathbf a=(\mathbf a+\mathbf d)\times \mathbf a
=\mathbf a\times\mathbf a+\mathbf d\times\mathbf a
=\mathbf d\times\mathbf a.
\]
Given \(\mathbf c\times\mathbf a=\mathbf b\), we have
\[
\|\mathbf d\times\mathbf a\|=\|\mathbf b\|=3.
\]
Using the cross product inequality,
\[
\|\mathbf d\times\mathbf a\|\le \|\mathbf d\|\|\mathbf a\|=2\|\mathbf d\|.
\]
Thus
\[
3\le 2\|\mathbf d\| \implies \|\mathbf d\|\ge \frac32.
\]
So
\[
\|\mathbf c-\mathbf a\|\ge \frac32.
\]
Equality occurs when \(\mathbf d\perp \mathbf a\), so the smallest possible value is \(\frac32\).

The answer is \(\boxed{\frac32}\).
